fields.Name: Sales: Bookings by Owner
fields.UserQuestion: Whose number is this — bookings credited to the deal owner, each deal counted once?
fields.Description: ATTRIBUTION BASIS: OWNER-ROLE FILTER, every deal counted exactly once. This is the "bookings by AE" question and it is the one to use for any figure that must reconcile — a board number, a commission input, an accounting tie-out. Its pair is "Sales: Deal Involvement by Rep", which is attribution-weighted and does NOT sum to bookings. Master plan §9.4: "There is no safe default that works for both." ADDITIVITY: every money column and count here totals correctly across rows, because the IsOwnerRole filter puts each deal on exactly one row. WinRateByCount is a ratio and does not average across rows.
fields.TechnicalDescription: Grain: DealTeamMember, filtered to DealRole.IsOwnerRole = 1 — a FLAG. Without that filter a deal with an AE, an SE and an SDR contributes its amount three times, which is the double-count §9.4 names. Deliberately does NOT read Deal.OwnerEmployeeID: that is a denormalised stamp derived from this same team row, and CLAUDE.md makes DealTeamMember the source of truth for membership. Date dimension: ActualCloseDate.

_comments: PARAMETERS ARE DERIVED BY MJ, NOT DECLARED HERE -- and the authored detail is kept below.
They were declared as relatedEntities['MJ: Query Parameters'], and that made this whole
directory unseedable on a fresh database. MJ derives parameters from the SQL when the query is
created; the declared rows then collided with them on the UNIQUE (QueryID, Name) index -- 18
violations, whole-transaction rollback, 0 of 16 queries landing, byte-identical on a retry.
That was KI-25, and it cost every fresh install its dashboard.
Removing the declarations lets MJ derive them: names and IsRequired come out identical. Type
degrades from date to string on the period parameters, which is harmless here because
QueryForecastSource passes them as ISO date-only STRINGS on purpose -- 'a full timestamp would
invite a query to compare a date column against an instant'. What would genuinely have been
lost is the authored Description and SampleValue, so they are preserved verbatim:
CompanyID (string)
Selling company. Omit for every company. Deal.CompanyID is server-stamped from the pipeline, so it is always present and never needs a fallback.
PipelineID (string)
One pipeline. Omit for all pipelines.
PeriodStart (date)
Inclusive start of the window. Omit for no lower bound.
PeriodEnd (date)
Inclusive end of the window. Omit for no upper bound.
